newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police arrest man in child sex probe.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police arrest man in child sex probe.

text.p: Belgian police arrested a man on Tuesday in connection with investigations into the disappearance of a nine-year-old Moroccan girl in Brussels four years ago.

The investigating magistrate in the Belgian town, Neufchateau, which has been the centre of investigations into the disappearance of several children since mid-August, said a former suspect in the case, Jacques Genevoix, had been arrested.
Genevoix was a suspect after Loubna Benaissa disappeared in August 1992 on the way to local shops, but it was only recently fresh evidence involving him came to light, Belgian police say.

The tempo of investigations into several missing children gained new impetus three months ago following the arrest of convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux and the subsequent rescue of two young girls and discovery of the bodies of four more.

The parents of the dead girls, Julie Lejeune, Melissa Russo, Eefje Lambrecks and An Marchal as well as the family of Loubna and the mother of another missing girl, Elizabeth Brichet, have led a campaign to make sure the investigations continue.
In October some 250,000 people marched through Brussels in a show of support for the victims and their families.

Dutroux, his second wife Michelle Martin, as well as suspected accomplices Michel Nihoul, Michel Lelievre and Mikael Diakostavrianos were arrested in August. They remain in jail while investigations continue.
No link has been established between Dutroux and Genevoix.
